summary: Replacing a failed system disk is rebuilt for the Nex Core image layout, Core first. When one disk of a two-disk host fails and an operator fits a blank disk, Core (internal/hostimage Host.ReplaceDisk, run by the agent on a goroutine of its own) revalidates the selected disk against a fresh observation, refuses the disk the running system started from and any non-blank disk without the typed erase confirmation, lays the surviving disk's identical GPT (nex-esp, slots A and B with their verity partitions, nex-data, nex-bios) on the replacement, copies the surviving disk's slots after verifying their whole dm-verity hash tree and verifies the copy read back from the medium, formats the boot partition once and fills it from the booted one through the host's boot method (systemd-boot and a firmware boot entry on UEFI, GRUB files plus grub-install on BIOS), and adds the replacement's nex-data partition to the md mirror with mdadm --add. The work is one durable record (<agent state dir>/system-disk/replace.json) keyed by request ID: the GPT disk GUID it writes is how a continued attempt recognises the disk as its own, so a replayed, retried (new request ID, same disk), interrupted or restarted replacement converges and never repeats a destructive step. A new disk lock serialises it with the update steps and the boot-partition sync. The Controller route POST /api/v1/hosts/{id}/system-disk and the capability host-system-disk-replace-v1 return in the same shape as before, without the array field; the host hardware report gains the optional system_disk member (the disk the host runs from and the replacement record with the kernel's resync progress). The host panel's Storage tab regains a Replace disk action.

guide.reason: A new operator workflow: reading the system disk mirror on a host's Storage tab and replacing a failed disk, including the typed erase confirmation, what Nex Core does in which order, how it continues after an interruption, every refusal, and the limits (not run on real disks).

api.reason: POST /api/v1/hosts/{id}/system-disk is an admin-authenticated, CSRF-protected route relaying the durable managed command host-system-disk-replace (SystemDiskReplaceRequest), gated on the host-system-disk-replace-v1 capability; the host hardware report is a changed contract in the same slice, gaining the optional system_disk member. Both sides are implemented, with the refusals, the replay and retry rules, the lock against update steps and the interruption behaviour in the reference.

roadmap.reason: Rebuilds a feature of the immutable Nex Core plan (D3: repair is re-lay GPT, copy verity-verified slots, mdadm --add data) as planned; no published milestone changed status.

state.reason: The mirror, the slots and the boot partitions are the host's own and nothing about them is pool-scoped. The Controller keeps only the task row it keeps for every host command.
state.record: The disks themselves (GPT, slots, boot partitions, md superblocks) and the host's replacement record /var/lib/nex-core-agent/system-disk/replace.json (request ID, selected disk, the GPT disk GUID the operation writes, boot-partition progress flags, phase, status, error, times).
state.recovery: Nothing to re-enter. A fresh Controller reads system_disk and md_arrays from the host's hardware report as soon as the host reconnects; an unfinished replacement continues by itself after a restart of Core.

verification.method: Go unit tests on file-backed disks with a fake block layer and a simulated md sysfs (WSL, go test ./internal/hostimage/... ./internal/protocol/... and the focused agent and controller tests; go vet; the hostimage and agent replacement tests also under -race), plus python3 scripts/generate_api.py, the API contract tests and python3 scripts/check_docs.py --worktree. Covered: both boot methods; the full rebuild; a power cut at every named step, retried with the same and with a new request ID; refusal of the running disk (also through an alias), of non-blank disks without the erase confirmation, of undersized disks, of a healthy, rebuilding, missing or non-RAID1 mirror, of a corrupt running slot, of an unblessed boot entry and of a wrong root hash; a corrupt previous slot skipped; a recorded failure continued by a new request; the disk lock against update steps and the boot-partition sync; agent admission, refusals, replay, the still-running answer, resumption after a restart and the report; the Controller relay, replay, refusals and CSRF. NOT verified: no real disk, md array, firmware boot or grub-install was exercised and the dialog was not walked through in a browser; no lab was run.
